learning_objective: 🧱 Understand how animal cells organize into specialized tissues—the building blocks that form organs and drive complex biological machines!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Animal bodies are made of just four basic tissue types: Epithelial (covering/lining), Connective (support/transport), Muscular (movement), and Neural (control/communication).

Tightly packed cells that act as a barrier. Squamous epithelium is flat (found in lungs for diffusion), Cuboidal is cube-like (kidney tubes for secretion), and Columnar is tall (stomach/intestine lining).

The most abundant tissue, it links and supports other tissues. It ranges from soft (Loose connective tissue like adipose/fat), to tough (tendons and ligaments), to rigid (cartilage and bone), to fluid (blood).

Cells that can contract. Skeletal muscle is striated and voluntary (attached to bones). Smooth muscle is non-striated and involuntary (walls of stomach/blood vessels). Cardiac muscle is striated, involuntary, and only found in the heart.

Responsible for sensing stimuli and rapidly transmitting signals. Neurons are the excitable cells that carry the electrical signals, while neuroglial cells protect, support, and make up the remaining bulk of the brain.

fun_activity.title: 💪 Control Your Muscles
fun_activity.instructions: Try to move your arm. You can, right? That's your 'Skeletal/Voluntary' muscle at work. Now, try to tell your stomach to digest faster or your heart to stop beating for 5 seconds. You can't! Those are 'Smooth' and 'Cardiac' involuntary muscles controlled automatically by your brain.

exam_tips: 📌 Distinguish between Tendons (connects Muscle to Bone) and Ligaments (connects Bone to Bone). Remember 'MTB' (Muscle-Tendon-Bone).
📌 Cardiac muscle cells uniquely have 'intercalated discs' (communication junctions) that allow the cells to contract together as a single unit.
📌 Adipose tissue is a type of loose connective tissue specialized to store fats; it acts as an insulator.
quick_recap: ⭐ Simple epithelium consists of a single layer of cells, while compound epithelium (like skin) has multiple layers for protection.
⭐ Blood is the only fluid connective tissue; it contains plasma, RBCs, WBCs, and platelets.
⭐ Neuroglia make up more than half the volume of neural tissue in our bodies, acting as support cells for neurons.
